question:
A 76-year-old woman presents with a 6-month history of bladder pain and dysuria. Her medical history
includes a 50-pack year smoking history and excessive consumption of caffeine and alcohol. Previous
treatment with intravesical instillations for bladder pain syndrome, diagnosed by her gynecologist, has
been unsuccessful. Her urine culture shows no growth. What should be the next appropriate step in
evaluating this patient? Answer Choices: (A) Multimodal pain management (B) Cystoscopy to rule out
malignancy (C) Referral to urology for consideration of neuromodulation therapy (D) Intravenous
pyelogram to evaluate for ureteral obstruction (E) Empiric trial of antibiotics for suspected UTI (F) MRI
of the pelvis to evaluate for structural abnormalities (G) Urinalysis with microscopy (H) Repeat urine
culture with extended panel testing (I) Serum creatinine to assess for renal dysfunction (J) Behavioral

modification including decreasing caffeine/alcohol and smoking cessation
 A. Multimodal pain management
B. Urinalysis with microscopy
C. Cystoscopy to rule out malignancy
D. Repeat urine culture with extended panel testing
E. Serum creatinine to assess for renal dysfunction
F. Intravenous pyelogram to evaluate for ureteral obstruction
G. MRI of the pelvis to evaluate for structural abnormalities
H. Empiric trial of antibiotics for suspected UTI
I. Referral to urology for consideration of neuromodulation therapy
J. Behavioral modification including decreasing caffeine/alcohol and smoking cessation
